summary: The main article describes the first palladium-catalyzed thiocarbonylation of alkenes using CO2 as a carbonyl source. It includes optimization tables, substrate scope schemes for alkenes and thiols, and mechanistic studies including in situ NMR and DFT calculations.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Palladium-catalyzed carbonylation to produce thioesters.
items.description: Comparison of previous work using CO with the current work using CO2 for the synthesis of branched thioesters.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Condition optimization for thiocarbonylation of styrene a
items.description: Optimization of catalysts, ligands, and reductants for the reaction of styrene with n-butanethiol under CO2.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Synthesis of branched thioesters by thiocarbonylation of alkenes.
items.description: Substrate scope for various alkenes (styrenes, internal olefins, basic substrates) and thiols using the optimized Pd/L1 system.

items.heading: Scheme 3
items.caption: Application study.
items.description: Synthetic applications including the synthesis of naproxen and an estrone derivative, as well as a gram-scale reaction.

items.heading: Scheme 4
items.caption: Experimental studies on the mechanism.
items.description: Mechanistic experiments including alkene insertion tests, control experiments with CO/HCOOH, and 13C labeling studies.

items.heading: Scheme 5
items.caption: Plausible reaction pathways for thiocarbonylation using CO2.
items.description: Proposed catalytic cycle showing the direct CO2 insertion path (path a) and the CO-mediated path (path b).
